      Before the water

      Mara has four villagers to bring home and a medicine chest to keep dry. The ferry is pinned. The causeway is broken. The Keeper is still sorting herbs.

      The crossing is the first part. What reaches shelter changes the next morning's relief work. At noon, another village asks for help: a boat, or the person who knows the channel.

      “Don't tell me we'll get everything out unless you've looked at what we can carry.”— Mara

        KEEP THE FLOOD IN VIEW

        Before you set out

        Pack two different items. Rope speeds one rescue, secures the ferry or makes a temporary crossing. Timber repairs the road or reinforces the hull. Oil signals the roof when the Waystone is dark.

        You have nine beats, including talk and travel. Each choice lists its cost. The roof workers leave for refuge at beat 6; Iven leaves the jetty at beat 5. Completing a rescue on its deadline succeeds. Reading, loading and unloading take no time.

        The Keeper can provide light for the causeway. You can leave for the ferry without agreement. Time spent talking is still time lost to the flood.

        On the ferry, people and medicine share cargo slots. Iven steers faster with more capacity. The current repeats slack → pull → surge: pull damages hull; surge damages it more and spoils exposed medicine. A guide line protects both; timber protects only the hull.

        The morning follows your night ending. Six work shifts compete for clinic supplies, isolated people, grain and sowing seed. Dry medicine is needed by shift 3; the wagon leaves at shift 6. A repaired road, retained ferry and Iven change load capacity and work costs. The ridge trail always offers a slow fallback.

        The noon courier follows the morning. Hear the people actually present, then keep local resources, lend a ready ferry or accept Iven’s own offer to guide. A loan changes the local route or its pace; a return deadline stays an obligation to check. Speaking takes no work shifts.

        Work until dusk. Four afternoon shifts use the transport and crew left locally. Finish deliveries, contact late clinic callers or plant with Senn. A promised return is still unverified at dusk.

        Your last accepted choice is saved locally. Save file exports the journey; Load file restores it on another browser. If storage is unavailable, file saves still work. No account or network is needed after the page loads.
